name: sbrk
description: brk() and sbrk() change the location of the program break, which defines the end of the process's data segment. Increasing the break allocates memory, while decreasing it deallocates memory. brk() sets the break to a specific address, and sbrk() adjusts it by a given increment.

parameters.name: addr
parameters.description: The desired new end of the data segment for brk()

parameters.name: increment
parameters.description: The number of bytes to increment the break by for sbrk()

return_value.success: brk() returns 0; sbrk() returns the previous program break
return_value.failure: Returns -1 or (void*)-1 on error, with errno set to ENOMEM

errors.description: The process would exceed its maximum data size or there is insufficient memory

bugs: The glibc wrapper for brk() differs from the kernel syscall behavior; various systems use different types for sbrk()'s argument. It is recommended to use malloc(3) instead for portability.
